nodes.name: Electrodeposition of Ni(Cu)VOx
nodes.procedure: The NF was firstly ultrasonicated in 5 M HCl solution for 10 min to remove the NiO layer, rinsed subsequently with water and ethanol, and then dried in air. The electrodeposition was conducted in an electrolyte containing 0.5 M NiSO₄, 12.5 mM CuSO₄, 7 mM NH₄VO₃, and 0.5 M H₃BO₃, by dissolving each chemical in 50 mL Milli-Q water under sonication and the electrodeposition then was carried out with a CHI 760D electrochemical workstation at -2.0 V (vs. SCE) for 600 s at room temperature.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni(Cu)VOx shows a small broad peak at 44.44° indicating poor crystallization and fine metallic Ni nanoparticles of 4.6 nm. Ni and Ni(Cu) show crystalline fcc Ni peaks at 44.44°, 51.26°, 76.35° while NiVOx shows vanished Ni peaks indicating highly disordered structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The crystal structures of the prepared catalysts were characterized by X-ray diffraction (XRD). As shown in Supplementary Fig. 4, the XRD patterns for Ni and Ni(Cu) are all crystalline with three main diffraction peaks at 2θ = 44.44°, 51.26°, and 76.35°, assigning to (111), (200), and (220) planes of face-centered cubic (fcc) Ni ... For Ni(Cu)VOx, a small and broad peak at 44.44° was observed, which suggests the poor crystallization and the formation of fine metallic Ni nanoparticles (NPs), as well as that a portion of Ni crystalline structures were restored with the incorporation of Cu. The size of Ni(Cu)VOx NPs was calculated to be 4.6 nm according to Scherrer equation...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni(Cu)VOx shows fine nanoparticles around 5 nm while Ni and Ni(Cu) show much larger crystals.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images show fine NPs with a size around 5 nm were obtained for Ni(Cu)VOx (Fig. 1b and Supplementary Fig. 6), while much larger crystals were observed for Ni and Ni(Cu)...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni(Cu)VOx shows fine NPs of 4-5 nm with discernible and undecipherable lattice fringes indicating poor crystallization, d-spacing of 0.202 nm corresponding to (111) plane of fcc Ni.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The transmission electron microscopy (TEM) image also shows fine Ni(Cu)VOx NPs having the size of 4-5 nm (Fig. 1c). It is noteworthy that discernible and undecipherable lattice fringe coexist, meaning these NPs are poorly crystallized. A closer investigation of the HRTEM result shows d-spacing of 0.202 nm (Fig. 1d), corresponding to (111) plane of fcc Ni.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM-EDS mapping shows uniform distribution of Ni, Cu, V, and O in Ni(Cu)VOx.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The typical TEM-EDS mapping shows the uniform distribution of Ni, Cu, V, and O (Fig. 1e–h).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni(Cu)VOx shows metallic Ni (Ni2p3/2 852.8 eV, Ni2p1/2 870.0 eV) with partial Ni2+ (~855.9 eV) due to VOx, metallic Cu (Cu2p3/2 932.8 eV, Cu2p1/2 952.6 eV), VOx with V5+ (517.1 eV) and V4+ (516.2 eV). NiVOx shows higher Ni oxidation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For Ni2p, the binding energy at 852.8 eV (Ni2p3/2 line) and 870.0 eV (Ni2p1/2 line) with peak split spin–orbit components of 17.2 eV, illustrate the formation of metallic Ni. In addition, the peak at ~855.9 eV is attributed to Ni2+, indicating Ni is partially oxidized as a result of deposited VOx ... The Cu2p shows the Cu 2p3/2 at 932.8 eV and Cu 2p1/2 at 952.6 eV ... The binding energies for V2p3/2 show two peaks at 517.1 eV (V5+) and 516.2 eV (V4+) ... For NiVOx, a higher oxidation degree of Ni was observed.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni(Cu)VOx on FTO shows Cu/Ni = 0.114 and V/Ni = 0.029 molar ratio; on NF shows Cu/Ni = 0.120 and V/Ni = 0.034.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The doped Cu and V were determined to be Cu/Ni = 0.114 and V/Ni = 0.029 (molar ratio) by inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES). In order to confirm that the active materials loaded on FTO and NF are the same, we tested the Ni(Cu)VOx powder scraped from NF by ICP-OES. The doped Cu and V were determined to be Cu/Ni = 0.120 and V/Ni = 0.034 (molar ratio), respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni(Cu)VOx shows Brunauer–Emmett–Teller specific surface area of 34.232 m² g⁻¹, highest among tested samples.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Apart from ECSA, we also measured the Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) specific surface area of Ni, Ni(Cu), NiVOx and Ni(Cu)VOx samples with 17.988, 26.614, 18.994, and 34.232 m² g⁻¹, respectively (Supplementary Fig. 20 and Supplementary Note 4).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge shows shift to higher energy in Ni(Cu)VOx indicating partial oxidation of Ni lattice by VOx; Cu K-edge shows Cu close to Cu⁰; V K-edge shows oxidation state between 4+ and 5+ with pre-edge shift indicating Ni-O-VOx interaction; EXAFS shows VOx dampens Ni lattice and no direct V-Ni bond but V-O with Ni-O-VOx bridging.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ni, Cu, and V K-edge XAS were carried out ... Fig. 3a shows the Ni K-edge spectra of the samples compared to Ni foil and NiO references. Adding VOx to the structure leads to a notable shift of the Ni K-edge positions towards higher energy, indicating that on average the material is more oxidized ... The XANES spectra of the materials at the Cu K-edge indicate that copper is close to Cu⁰ (Fig. 3b). The V K-edge XANES data ... suggest vanadium has an oxidation state between 4+ and 5+, consistent with the XPS results ... The Fourier transform (FT) and the EXAFS at Ni K-edge data show that the introduction of VOx causes a substantial dampening to the Ni K-edge EXAFS ... From simulations of the EXAFS at V K-edge, there were no direct V–Ni/Cu bond in Ni(Cu)VOx, but a well fit with a V–O bond was achieved, which is consistent with the interaction between Ni and V as bridged by Ni–O–VOx.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni(Cu)VOx shows charge transfer resistance Rct = 9.4 Ω, much smaller than control samples, indicating fast charge transfer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 2f shows Cu doping can accelerate the electron transfer during HER and the charge transfer resistance (Rct) in Ni(Cu)VOx Rct = 9.4 Ω, is much smaller than that of the control samples, revealing fast charge transfers and minimal parasitic ohmic losses during HER.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni(Cu)VOx shows highest double-layer capacitance Cdl among tested samples, indicating largest electrochemically active surface area (ECSA).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electrochemical surface area (ECSA) was evaluated using double-layer capacitance (Cdl), determined from CV at different scan rates. The Cdl value of Ni(Cu)VOx is the highest among the tested samples (Supplementary Figs. 17 and 18 and Supplementary Note 3).
